title: Grade 6 French — Thu, May 21
description: Les jours, mois et saisons (Days, Months, Seasons) — Day 4 of 5
subject: french

questions.question: What is Monday in French?
questions.explanation: 'Lundi' = Monday. The days: lundi(Mon), mardi(Tue), mercredi(Wed), jeudi(Thu), vendredi(Fri), samedi(Sat), dimanche(Sun).

questions.question: What day of the week is 'jeudi'?
questions.explanation: 'Jeudi' = Thursday. Mnemonic: 'Jeudi' sounds like 'Jove's day' (Jupiter/Zeus's day) — Thursday in many languages.

questions.question: In French, what is special about writing days of the week?
questions.explanation: Unlike English, French days of the week are NOT capitalized: lundi, mardi, mercredi... The same applies to months.

questions.question: How do you say 'on Mondays' (every Monday) in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le lundi' = on Mondays (every Monday). Adding the article 'le' before a day makes it habitual: 'Le lundi, je vais à l'école' = On Mondays I go to school.

questions.question: What is June in French?
questions.explanation: 'Juin' = June. The months: janvier(Jan), février(Feb), mars(Mar), avril(Apr), mai(May), juin(Jun), juillet(Jul), août(Aug), septembre(Sep), octobre(Oct), novembre(Nov), décembre(Dec).

questions.question: Which month is 'août'?
questions.explanation: 'Août' = August. Pronunciation: the 't' is silent in casual speech ('oo'). Some pronounce it 'oot'.

questions.question: How do you say 'in January' in French?
questions.explanation: 'En janvier' = in January. Use 'en' before months (not 'dans' or 'au'): en mars, en octobre.

questions.question: What is 'le printemps'?
questions.explanation: 'Le printemps' = Spring. The four seasons: le printemps(Spring), l'été(Summer), l'automne(Autumn), l'hiver(Winter).

questions.question: How do you say 'in summer' in French?
questions.explanation: 'En été' = in summer. Use 'en' for seasons starting with a vowel: en été, en automne. Use 'en' for hiver too: en hiver. Only 'au printemps' is different.

questions.question: Which is correct for 'in spring'?
questions.explanation: 'Au printemps' = in spring. This is the exception — spring uses 'au' (à + le), unlike the other seasons which use 'en'.

questions.question: How do you say your birthday date: 'My birthday is on March 15th'?
options: Mon anniversaire est le quinze mars
Mon anniversaire est en mars quinze
Mon anniversaire est au quinze mars
questions.explanation: 'Mon anniversaire est le quinze mars' = My birthday is on the 15th of March. Structure: le + [number] + [month] (no 'st/nd/th' — just the cardinal number).

questions.question: What does 'Aujourd'hui, c'est mercredi.' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Aujourd'hui' = today. 'C'est' = it is. 'Aujourd'hui, c'est mercredi' = Today is Wednesday.

questions.question: How would you say 'the first of January' (New Year's Day) in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le premier janvier' = January 1st. For the first day of any month, use 'premier' (not 'un'). For all other dates, use cardinal numbers: le deux, le trois, etc.

questions.question: 'Quel jour sommes-nous?' is asking:
questions.explanation: 'Quel jour sommes-nous?' = 'What day is it today?' (literally 'What day are we?'). Answer: 'Nous sommes lundi' or 'C'est lundi.'

questions.question: How do you say 'See you on Friday' in French?
questions.explanation: 'À vendredi' = See you on Friday (literally 'Until Friday'). Similarly: à lundi (see you Monday), à demain (see you tomorrow).
